title: Vocabulary in Context
tagline: Year 2 — Working out the meaning of an unfamiliar word from the clues around it

introduction.overview: You will often meet a word you do not know. The sentence around it usually gives clues to its meaning: a definition, a synonym or antonym, an example, a contrast, or the general sense of the passage. Vocabulary-in-context questions train you to use these clues and to choose the meaning that fits. This builds the habit of learning new words from reading.
introduction.placementRelevance: Vocabulary-in-context questions are commonly asked in the verbal ability section of company aptitude rounds, especially inside reading comprehension passages.
introduction.realWorldContext: When you read reports, articles or documents with new words, context clues let you keep reading and understand without a dictionary.

learningObjectives: Recognise the main types of context clues
Use contrast and comparison words to infer meaning
Use examples and explanations given in the sentence
Check that the chosen meaning fits the whole sentence
Use word parts and tone when clues are weak

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Look for contrast words (but, unlike), explanation words (that is, because), examples (such as) and the positive or negative tone of the sentence.

coreDefinitions: Context clue: information in the surrounding text that points to a word's meaning.
Definition clue: the sentence defines the word directly.
Contrast clue: the sentence contrasts the word with its opposite (unlike, but, however).
Example clue: examples illustrate the word.
Inference clue: the general situation suggests the meaning.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The author wants to be understood, so the sentence usually helps. Ask: what idea does the rest of the sentence express? The unknown word is probably part of the same idea or its opposite.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Cover the word and guess a simple word that would fit. Then match your guess to an option. Finally, substitute the option back and check that the sentence still makes sense.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Definition clue
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Look for that is, means, called.
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: a tentative explanation yet to be tested = hypothesis

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Contrast clue
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: But, unlike, however signal an opposite
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Unlike his gregarious brother, who loved parties, he stayed alone

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Example clue
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Examples show the kind of thing

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Cause clue
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: He was frail, so he could hardly lift a cup

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Tone clue
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Choose a word with the same tone.

mainNarrative: Start with the nearest clues. In "The weather was so inclement that the match was cancelled; heavy rain and strong winds lashed the ground", the second part describes the weather, so inclement means stormy or harsh.
Use contrast words. "Unlike his gregarious brother, who loved parties, Anil preferred to stay alone" tells you gregarious is the opposite of preferring to stay alone: sociable.
Use examples and actions. A man who saved every rupee and never wasted money is frugal. A person who forgave late arrivals and did not punish anyone is lenient.
Use the situation. "Because the instructions were ambiguous, each student interpreted them differently" means the instructions could be understood in more than one way.
Finally substitute the meaning into the sentence. If it reads naturally and fits the tone, the choice is right.

deepDiveAspects.title: Prefix and root help
deepDiveAspects.content: Unprecedented = un (not) + precedent (something earlier). Nothing like it had happened before. Word parts support the context.

deepDiveAspects.title: Avoid sound-alikes
deepDiveAspects.content: Do not choose a word because it sounds like the target. Meaning in context is what counts.

solvedExamples.title: Contrast clue
solvedExamples.question: Unlike his gregarious brother, who loved parties, Anil preferred to stay alone. What does "gregarious" mean?

steps.title: Clue
steps.explanation: Anil prefers to be alone; the brother is unlike him.

solvedExamples.commonTrap: Choosing an option similar to Anil.

solvedExamples.title: Example clue
solvedExamples.question: He was frugal; he saved every rupee and never wasted money. What does "frugal" mean?

steps.title: Examples
steps.explanation: Saved every rupee, never wasted money.

solvedExamples.title: Cause clue
solvedExamples.question: The old man was so frail that he could hardly lift a cup. What does "frail" mean?

steps.title: Result
steps.explanation: He could hardly lift a cup.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Find the clue, guess the meaning, match it to an option, and substitute to check.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options with the wrong tone first.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Most sentences contain a direct clue.

easy.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "inclement".
"The weather was so inclement that the match was cancelled; heavy rain and strong winds lashed the ground."
easy.explanation: Heavy rain and strong winds describe harsh, stormy weather.

easy.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "frugal".
"He was frugal; he saved every rupee and never wasted money."
easy.explanation: Saving every rupee shows care with money.

easy.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "lucid".
"The teacher's lucid explanation made the topic easy to understand."
easy.explanation: An explanation that makes things easy to understand is clear.

intermediate.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "gregarious".
"Unlike his gregarious brother, who loved parties, Anil preferred to stay alone."
intermediate.explanation: Loving parties contrasts with staying alone: sociable.

intermediate.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "rhetoric".
"The politician's speech was full of rhetoric, but it contained no concrete plans."
intermediate.explanation: But signals that the speech lacked concrete plans, so it was fine words without substance.

intermediate.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "keen".
"The detective's keen observation, noticing even the smallest detail, solved the case."
intermediate.explanation: Noticing the smallest detail shows sharpness.

advanced.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "hypothesis".
"The scientist's hypothesis, a tentative explanation yet to be tested, was published."
options: a proposed explanation to be tested
advanced.correctAnswer: a proposed explanation to be tested
advanced.explanation: The sentence itself defines it as a tentative explanation yet to be tested.

advanced.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "ambiguous".
"Because the instructions were ambiguous, each student interpreted them differently."
options: open to more than one meaning
advanced.correctAnswer: open to more than one meaning
advanced.explanation: Different interpretations suggest the instructions could be understood in more than one way.

placementStyle.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "meagre".
"The company's meagre profits barely covered the salaries."
placementStyle.explanation: Barely covering salaries shows the profits were very small.

placementStyle.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "eloquent".
"Her eloquent speech, fluent and persuasive, won the audience."
placementStyle.explanation: The sentence describes it as fluent and persuasive.

placementStyle.question:
Use the clues in the sentence to decide the meaning of the word "animosity".
"The rivals' animosity was clear; they refused even to shake hands."
placementStyle.explanation: Refusing to shake hands shows hostility.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I use an example clue?
Can I use a contrast clue?
